findings.title: retryCount deletion branch is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The `deleteMany` uses `OR: [{method: SMS, scheduledDate lte now}, {retryCount > 1}]`. The second branch has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and no `scheduled`/`scheduledDate` condition, so any WorkflowReminder row of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) whose retryCount exceeds 1 will be deleted by this SMS cron job. Today only this file increments retryCount, but the column is on the shared WorkflowReminder model and any other code path (or a future email/whatsapp retry implementation) that increments it will have its reminders silently destroyed by the SMS scheduler. The retryCount condition should be conjoined with `method: SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`).

findings.title: Reminders skipped due to empty message or missing sendTo never increment retryCount
findings.body: The retryCount increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)`. When `sendTo` is null/empty (e.g. booking has no smsReminderNumber and step action is not SMS_NUMBER) or the computed message is empty, neither the success nor the failure branch runs, so retryCount stays 0 and the reminder is re-fetched and re-skipped on every cron run until scheduledDate passes — exactly the 'kept scheduling until date is reached' behavior this PR claims to fix. These reminders should either be deleted or have retryCount incremented so they are purged.

findings.title: retryCount increment uses stale in-memory value
findings.body: The update writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` based on the value read when the batch was queried, rather than an atomic `increment: { retryCount: 1 }`. If the cron job runs concurrently (overlapping invocations or a manual trigger while the scheduled run is in progress), increments can be lost, so a reminder can fail more than twice before being deleted. Use `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` instead.

findings.title: Exhausted reminders are silently deleted with no audit or notification
findings.body: When a reminder exceeds the retry limit it is hard-deleted from the WorkflowReminder table. There is no log, no record of which booking/step failed, and no signal to the workflow owner, so users silently stop receiving SMS reminders (e.g. invalid phone numbers) with no way to diagnose it. Consider logging the deleted reminder ids or soft-cancelling (setting `cancelled`) instead of deleting, and/or notifying the workflow owner.
